intro:
Transylvania's seat 2 (left of the dealer): drawn facing the viewer's right, as the game shows him. Built the way the Green Knight is (`art-tools/pose_rig.py`), a quarter bigger: he is the table's giant.

His look, from his character file and Shelley: eight feet tall; long, lustrous black hair; yellow skin stretched over muscle; watery eyes nearly the colour of their sockets (drawn pale grey, so they still read); straight black lips; a good coat never cut for him. Articulate, well read, sad, gentle until he is not. His prop is a small battered copy of Paradise Lost in a very large hand, and where he puts it is the tell surface.

Ruled out (his character file): everything of Universal's 1931 design, which is still protected: no neck bolts, no flat-topped head, no green skin, no stitches or forehead scar, no grunting, no stiff-armed walk. Layout from Lancelot's character sheet, style from the Headless Horseman's approved character sheet: the GOTHIC style, from Transylvania on (the owner).

Tags (MOTION-SPEC.md): his three tells, each beside the idle it hides among: setting his book face-down on the table (strong) beside reading a line of Milton, lips moving (the book in both hands); turning a page he is not reading (weak) beside staring at his own hands; the table creaking under his grip (tilted) beside straightening a coat that was never made for him. 'Flinches from the firelight' is C4. B3 and D4 are the big win and the crushing loss; his hands are empty of cards and chips in every pose (the game moves them; the book is his own); knocked out, he says his line and fades from the chair, so no exit pose.

howto: One fresh ChatGPT chat for all six. The first prompt attaches TWO images, in this order: Lancelot's character sheet (`art-tools/lancelot_parts/sources/lancelot_sheet.png`) for the layout, then the Headless Horseman's approved character sheet (`art-tools/headless_horseman_parts/sources/headless_horseman_sheet.png`) for the style. character:
Character sheet for 2D animation rigging: the creature of Mary Shelley's Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus (1818), as Shelley describes him in the novel. Copy ONLY the LAYOUT of the FIRST attached sheet (what goes where): take NOTHING of its character. No plate armour, no gauntlets, no striped surcoat. Take the STYLE from the SECOND attached image.

The Monster: an ENORMOUS man, a head taller than any other man at the table and broad as a door, powerfully built; long, flowing, glossy BLACK hair falling past his ears to his collar; pale YELLOWISH skin, smooth, drawn a little thin over strong bones; a long, sombre, intelligent face; pale watery grey eyes with small dark pupils, deep-set; straight dark lips; white teeth. A good dark coat that was never cut for him: too tight across the huge shoulders, its sleeves too short so his big wrists show; a plain white shirt open at the collar. Sad, gentle, articulate, well read; dangerous only when wronged. His prop: a small, battered brown leather book (Paradise Lost), tiny in his huge hand. Nothing of Universal's 1931 film design: NO neck bolts, NO flat-topped or square head, NO green or grey skin, NO stitches, NO scars, NO heavy brow ridge, NO platform boots. Nothing from any film.

Pure white background (#FFFFFF). Every piece separate, with a closed dark outline and a wide gap all round it; nothing touches or overlaps. No text, no labels, no frames, no cast shadows.

The angle: a gentle three-quarter view, turned about 25 degrees from front-on, facing the viewer's right. Both eyes, the whole nose, the mouth and both shoulders clearly visible. NOT profile.

Draw, all facing the viewer's right, at the same size:
- Finished heads, each with the long hair, the neck and the top of the shirt collar: neutral, sad and calm; talking, mouth open mid-word; reading, eyes lowered, lips moving; flinching, eyes narrowed, turned a little away
- The torso in the tight dark coat: no head, cut off straight below the waist, the upper arms down to the elbows; NO forearms, NO hands
- Two forearms in the too-short coat sleeves, big wrists showing, lying on a table, pointing toward its centre, open at the elbow end
- On their own: the small battered brown book, open; the same book closed
- Four seated reference poses, waist up behind the curved edge of a round green poker table, forearms resting on its edge, hands apart, the book open in his left hand on the felt: neutral; the book set face-down on the felt, both hands flat beside it; turning a page with one big finger, eyes elsewhere; both hands gripping the table's edge hard, two short creak lines beside them

A: At rest: both forearms lying along the table's edge, his hands resting on the felt in front of him, a hand's width apart, relaxed and NOT touching, NOT laced, NOT overlapping; the small book held open in his left hand on the felt; a calm, sad look, mouth closed
Peeking at his cards: his right hand cupped low over the felt in front of him, thumb lifted a little, as if shielding something small; eyes down
Checking: one big finger of his right hand tapping the felt
Calling: his right hand flat, fingertips leading, pushing forward along the felt
Betting: his right hand pushed well forward along the felt, carefully
Folding: a gentle push of his right hand toward the middle of the table, palm down
B: All in: both hands pushing forward along the felt together (the book set down closed by his left elbow)
Showing: his right hand turning palm up from the felt, as if turning something over
A big win: both huge hands raised high above his head, a wondering, delighted smile, as if he cannot believe it (the book set down closed by his left elbow)
Setting his book face-down on the felt: the book lying open, face DOWN, spine up, under his left hand; his eyes on the viewer
Reading a line of Milton: the book held up open in both hands in front of his chest, eyes on the page, lips moving
Turning a page he is not reading: one big finger of his right hand turning a page of the open book in his left hand, his eyes NOT on the book, looking at the table
C: Staring at his own hands: both big hands lifted a little off the felt, palms up, the book set down closed by his left elbow, eyes on his hands, puzzled and sad
Gripping the table: both huge hands clamped on the table's edge, knuckles white, two short creak lines beside each hand, the book set down closed by his left elbow, face very still
Straightening his coat: his right hand tugging the too-tight lapel straight, shoulders hunched a little; left hand as at rest with the book
Flinching from the firelight: head turned away toward the right of the picture, eyes narrowed, his right forearm half raised against the light
Looking straight at the viewer, sad and steady; arms as at rest
Pushing his long black hair back from his face with his right hand
D: Talking: his right hand open and raised a little, palm up, explaining, mouth open mid-word
Facing a big bet: brows drawn down, very still, eyes fixed; arms as at rest
Lost a pot: head bowed, eyes closed; arms as at rest
A crushing loss: his face hidden in both huge hands, elbows on the table's edge (the book set down closed by his left elbow)
Down to two players: leaning in on both forearms, eyes on the viewer
A quiet laugh, surprised at himself, head tipped back a little, his right hand flat on his chest

style: STYLE, the most important rule: match the SECOND attached image (the Headless Horseman, from the same table) exactly: a GOTHIC GRAPHIC-NOVEL style for a grown-up card game, halfway between a bright cartoon and a dark painted illustration. Take NOTHING of his character: no armour, no pumpkin, no cloak. Keep what the game needs: a bold dark outline round every shape, big clear readable shapes, a silhouette that reads at a tiny size. Adult, realistic proportions (never a big head, never chibi, never cute); shading in three or four tones with deep, dramatic shadows and a warm rim light from candlelight; rich but MUTED colour, nothing candy-bright; cloth with real weight and heavy folds; a little texture in the shadows only. Serious and sombre. NOT a children's cartoon, NOT cute, NOT toy-like, NOT round and bouncy, NOT photoreal, NOT muddy or murky.
style_short: Keep the gothic graphic-novel style of the attached sheets and of the Headless Horseman's sheet: bold dark outlines, adult proportions, deep three- or four-tone shading, a warm candlelit rim light, rich muted colour; serious and sombre, NOT a children's cartoon, NOT cute.
